newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Cenbank sells dollar-indexed Treasury notes.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Cenbank sells dollar-indexed Treasury notes.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank sold Monday dollar-indexed National Treasury Notes (NTN-D) for a total face value of 980 million reais that it had held in its portfolio, dealers said.

The Bank sold 380 million reais of NTN-D notes that come due on Nov 1, 1997 and pay an annual yield of 10.60 percent. The Bank also sold 600 million reais of NTN-D notes coming due Mar 1, 1998 paying an annual yield of 10.79 percent.
Both series of NTN-Ds have a 24-month maturities and were part the Central Bank's portfolio.
Dealers said the auction was aimed at offering the market hedge opportunities and calming dollar futures markets, which have been nervous about the country's worsening trade figures.
Brazil posted a $1.787 billion trade deficit in December and a record $5.539 billion trade deficit in 1996. Forecasts for the January trade deficit are around $1.0 billion.
Players still remained concerned about how trade deficits could affect the current forex policy, dealers added.
